description: Hi, I’m Hema! I’m interested in space and health tech, and I’m building a calm, easy-to-use health dashboard for astronauts. It tracks sleep, heart rate and mood, and shows changes compared with each person’s own baseline. We already have a working prototype.
summary:
We developed a Crew Health Monitor prototype to help astronauts track their health and wellbeing during long space missions. Crew members can log sleep, heart rate, mood, energy, stress, and symptoms, then compare their entries with their own recent patterns. When something appears different from usual, the monitor provides a prompt to recheck the reading or contact the onboard medical officer.
Keeping these records in one place can help crew members notice changes and share relevant information with mission control. This matters because timely awareness of health concerns is especially important when a crew is far from Earth and medical support may be limited. The prototype uses simulated data and is for demonstration purposes; it is not a clinically validated medical device.
details:
The Crew Health Monitor is a prototype that helps astronauts keep track of their health during long space missions. They can log things like sleep, heart rate, mood, energy, stress, and symptoms, then see how their latest readings compare with their own recent patterns. If something has changed, the monitor prompts them to check the reading or follow up with the onboard medical officer.

The idea is to make it easier to spot changes and keep useful health information organized, especially when a crew is far from Earth and medical support is limited. The monitor uses each person’s own history to identify changes, keeps private notes separate, and lets users choose what information to share. It also treats missing readings as unknown rather than assuming everything is normal.

The prototype is designed to work without an account or network connection, and its data and sharing features are simulated. The project document doesn’t specify the programming languages or development tools used, and no special hardware is described. It is a demonstration project, not a clinically validated medical device.
